comments.text: If time/universe/reality is actually infinite, it means that there's unlimited possibilities of things happening. But it comes with a funny little paradox. If there's unlimited time there must be infinite ammount of possibilities and that means basically that the earth will explode out of nowhere one day but comeback instantly but there also would be a time when earth explodes out of nowhere and it doesn't ever come back. So basically infinite possibilities isn't possible. Infinite time therefore isn't possible. So we now have two choices... Either big bang theory is real or close to real and time began then and it ends someday to something or we live in a loop. What do I mean by a loop? I mean that we saw one point for example big bang, and decided that it was the "birth" of universe but actually it was the turning point of our loop, our world might've exploded due to human stupidity or something else and that's the point we thought was the start of the universe. So infinite time isn't possible if it's not a loop. But to think there's not time before time or time after time doesn't seem logical either. Since if time decided to stop now, there would be 100% chances of time becoming back sometime and that'd mean there was time before time ended and before it started again but there was nobody to measure that time.
